title: Provision persistence and integrity hooks can reenter verifier and regress rollback state
description: Fresh final timing robustness/security review: ProvisionVerifier.install and clear invoke external verify_integrity, persist_rollback_state, and persist_clear callbacks while holding a threading.RLock, which explicitly permits same-thread reentry. A one-shot persist hook can recursively install a higher version; after the inner commit returns, the outer lower-version install resumes and overwrites __rollback/__current, regressing the in-memory floor. Clear/install cross-reentry can likewise violate generation/current/cleared atomicity. Add an explicit non-reentrant transition guard covering verify/persist/commit/clear (or a transaction design with post-callback generation revalidation), fail closed on callback reentry without partial state mutation, and test v2 outer→v3 inner, install→clear, clear→install, callback exceptions, and concurrent non-reentrant callers.
notes: Also cover awaitable hooks: async persist_marker/persist_rollback_state/persist_clear return coroutine objects that are never awaited, yet current code treats them as durable success and issues/commits virgin, rollback, or cleared state. Reject coroutine functions and any awaitable return (closing coroutine objects), with no state mutation; add each hook case.
